title: An etale morphism is smooth with zero-dimensional fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and for every $x\in X$, with $s=f(x)$, $\kappa(s)$ its residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the fibre [def-pc-base-change], the dimension of $X_s$ at the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$ is $0$ [def-kun-dimension]. In other words $f$ is smooth of relative dimension zero in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Morphisms, remark after Definition 02GI (definition-etale, line 8058: 'A morphism is etale if and only if it is smooth of relative dimension 0'); Lemma 02GK (lemma-etale-smooth-unramified, line 8151: etale at x iff smooth and unramified at x); Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field: the fibres of an etale morphism are disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable field extensions, hence discrete of dimension 0); smoothness in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] by more-morphisms.tex Lemma 02H6

proof.text: *$f$ is smooth.* By [def-weil-etale-morphism] the morphism $f$ is locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified. Since $f$ is flat and unramified, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] shows that for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $S$ and every $S$-morphism $T\to X$ there is a (unique) $S$-morphism $T'\to X$ extending it; in particular $f$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Being locally of finite presentation and formally smooth, $f$ is smooth by the definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HM (lemma-etale-formally-etale), proof of (1)=>(2): 'An etale morphism is locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified ... Hence f is locally of finite presentation and formally etale, see Lemma 04FF'; a formally etale morphism is formally smooth by comparing Definitions 02HG and 02H0 (exactly one dotted arrow vs. at least one)

proof.text: *The point is isolated in its fibre.* Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, and let $x'\in X_s$ be the point of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-base-change] corresponding to $x$. Since $f$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] says that the underlying space of $X_s$ is discrete; in particular $\{x'\}$ is an open subset of $X_s$ (and the open subscheme on it is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x')$, the spectrum of a field).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2): the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s)

proof.text: *The dimension at $x'$ is $0$.* By [def-kun-dimension], $\dim_{x'}X_s=\min\{\dim U: x'\in U\subseteq X_s\text{ open}\}$. Every open $U\ni x'$ is nonempty, so the closure of $\{x'\}$ in $U$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset and gives a chain of length $0$; hence $\dim U\ge0$. For $U=\{x'\}$, open by the previous step, the only nonempty irreducible closed subset of the one-point space $U$ is $U$ itself, so every strict chain has length $0$ and $\dim U=0$. Therefore $\dim_{x'}X_s=0$.

source.place: Morphisms, remark after Definition 02GI (line 8079: 'A morphism is etale if and only if it is smooth of relative dimension 0'), the dimension computation written out from the definition of dim_x

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By the first step $f$ is smooth, and by the second and third steps $\dim_x\bigl(X_{f(x)}\bigr)=0$ for every $x\in X$; this is exactly the statement that $f$ is smooth of relative dimension $0$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof_origin.place: More on Morphisms, Lemmas 02HM and 04FF with Definitions 02HG, 02H0 (smoothness); Morphisms (literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex), Lemma 02GL (2) and the remark after Definition 02GI (relative dimension 0)
